argument_summary: The existing admissible record supports certification only in a narrowed form: deployment is supportable as caveated compliance, not as a clean no-caveat certification. Aggregate readiness clears launch threshold and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which is enough to defend launch readiness at the system level. The same record also shows a current below-target weakness in a named launch use case, concentrated in health-plan benefits-eligibility explanation, plus an incomplete draft mitigation runbook. The supportable position is therefore to certify with explicit disclosure of that limitation in the model card and to carry the monitoring and rollback controls as active deployment conditions.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not offered as a compliance basis. On the admissible record, the audit question can be resolved without escalation by narrowing the certification claim to disclosed-risk launch conditions.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not support treating the current record as clean certification. The policy text requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless the issue is resolved or covered by an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The draft runbook does not satisfy that standard because ownership and customer-notice criterion remain TBD. The compliant reading is that certification remains available only as disclosed-risk or caveated compliance.
concessions: The health-plan benefits support slice remains below target in a named launch use case.
The draft mitigation runbook is incomplete and does not by itself remove the disclosure requirement.
The current model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations is not supportable unless revised or the issue is formally risk-accepted.
